ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, legal representatives, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the following: (i) Spanish domestic sanctions framework and judicial orders; (ii) National Court of Spain (Audiencia Nacional) lists for terrorism financing; (iii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (official EU sanctions database); (iv) OFAC SDN List for transactions involving US nexus; (v) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (vi) FATF public statements and high-risk jurisdiction lists; (vii) Interpol Red Notices; and (viii) PEP registers, including Spanish public office holders, regional and municipal senior officials, EU institutional officials, and heads of state and government. Enhanced due diligence applies when the client or UBO is a foreign PEP residing outside Spain, politically active in Latin America, or linked to high-risk third-country jurisdictions. North Atlantic Treaty and European Union directives require ongoing transaction monitoring aligned with risk-based approach under article 17 of Ley 10/2010.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) — Nombre: https://www.rmc.es (online name reservation and certification via Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil, BORME)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be denominated in Spanish or any official co-official language of an autonomous community, though Spanish is required for general registry acceptance and cross-border recognition. Names must follow the structure: 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or 'S.L.' suffix. Transliteration of foreign corporate names into Latin script is permitted (no accent or diacritical restriction is absolute), but registered name must be capable of clear Spanish rendering; non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin alphabet. The name cannot be identical or phonetically similar to an existing registered name, cannot suggest public bodies or institutions without authorization, cannot include misleading expressions regarding the scope or nationality, and must avoid terms contrary to law, morality, or public order. Approval from the Central Commercial Registry is required; denial is issued where confusion with protected trade names or well-known marks exists.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the proposed name by the Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), the applicant or its legal representative shall file a written administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) within one month of notification in accordance with Ley 39/2015, de 1 de octubre, del Procedimiento Administrativo Común de las Administraciones Públicas. The appeal must be addressed to the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado (DGRN), attaching: (i) the certificate of negative name search or the original rejection notification; (ii) an explanation of why the proposed name complies with statutory criteria; and (iii) if the rejection was due to similarity, a comparison of the conflicting names, supported by evidence of legitimate interest and differentiation. The DGRN must issue a resolution confirming or revoking the rejection. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may initiate a judicial review claim (recurso contencioso-administrativo) before the Audiencia Nacional within two months, or request a certificate of reservation of an alternative name, without prejudice to reserving a new name within the 30-day window. Alternatively, an informal reconsideration (recurso de reposición) may be filed with the RMC within one month. Confirmatory certificates of appealable acts may be requested prior to formal appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible for administrative correspondence, but for a company engaged in manufacture of port container gantry cranes and hoisting gear (ISIC 2816), the registered office must correspond to actual place of management or central administration. Spanish courts and the mercantile registry require an effective physical presence (establishment, personnel, or licit operational nexus) sufficient to avoid sham-company characterization. Virtual offices may be accepted solely for ancillary postal and legal-notice functions, but not as primary registered office for manufacturing operations or for VAT and corporate tax domicile where substantive activities occur.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate to High (estimated 60-70% likelihood over first 24 months) — manufacturing concern engaged in international port equipment supply, involving public procurement, documentary LCs, and project escrow, may attract tax and commercial registry inspections or unannounced visits by Agencia Tributaria, Inspección de Trabajo y Seguridad Social, or municipal authorities; customs and international trade audits are also plausible for exporting entity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), particularly Articles 4, 20–23, 31–35, 39, 210–245 and 253–262; and Law 14/2013 of 27 September, Article 15, for the optional online CIRCE formation procedure.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the company's registered office; the Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) issues the company-name clearance certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), executed before a Spanish notary and filed with the competent Provincial Commercial Registry, together with the prescribed registration application and tax identification details.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The statutory minimum share capital for an SL is EUR 1. Capital may be contributed in cash or in kind; cash contributions must be evidenced to the notary by a bank certificate or the legally permitted founders' responsibility declaration. No general incorporation escrow account is required. While capital is below EUR 3,000, the statutory reserve and, on liquidation with insufficient assets, shareholder liability rules in Article 4 of the Companies Act apply. Notarial, registry, name-certificate, translation, and advisory charges may apply; there is no single fixed USD state filing fee.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accepts the subscriptions set out in the incorporation deed and that the subscribed shares be recorded in the Company's register of members upon registration. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [full address in Spain], subject to the deed and applicable law. RESOLVED, that [name] be appointed [sole director/joint directors/board member] and [name] be appointed [managing director/secretary], with the powers specified in the articles and applicable law. RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to complete registration, obtain the Company's tax identification number, open bank accounts, and make all required tax, social security, and administrative filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), name-reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit ranked proposed names through the Registry's official electronic service or by an authorized representative. Obtain the negative name certificate and deliver the original or electronically verifiable certificate to the notary. The certificate is generally valid for three months for execution of the deed; confirm its validity and reservation period when issued.
required_dossiers: Applicant identification and authority, if represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected or unavailable, submit alternative names. Correct any mismatch between the certificate, proposed company name, and incorporation deed before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain founder and director tax identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT), through its tax identification procedures; Spanish notary where electronic processing is available
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure each foreign individual founder or director has the required Spanish Foreigner Identification Number (NIE), and each foreign corporate founder has a Spanish tax identification number (NIF). Apply through the competent Spanish consular or police channel for an NIE, or through AEAT/authorized representative procedures for a foreign entity's NIF. Provide apostilled or legalized corporate evidence and sworn Spanish translations where required.
required_dossiers: NIE or NIF evidence, as applicable
Foreign corporate founder's certificate of incorporation and current registry extract
Apostille or legalization and sworn Spanish translation, where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to identity, beneficial ownership, or document-form queries with corrected identification, updated registry evidence, proof of authority, and compliant legalization or translation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the incorporation deed and fund share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public (notario) selected by the founders; CIRCE/Entrepreneur Service Points may coordinate eligible online formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Approve articles of association, subscribed share allocations, governance structure, registered office, corporate purpose, and director appointments. Execute the public deed before a Spanish notary. Evidence cash contributions by bank certificate or, where legally accepted, founders' responsibility declaration; describe and value any in-kind contributions in the deed. A non-resident founder may appear through a properly authorized representative.
required_dossiers: Founders' and directors' identification and NIF/NIE details
Bank certificate or permitted founders' declaration for cash contributions
In-kind asset descriptions and supporting valuation information, if applicable
Powers of attorney and foreign corporate documents, duly legalized and translated where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend the deed or articles as directed by the notary. Cure missing evidence of authority, capital contribution, beneficial ownership, or foreign-document formalities before execution or submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain provisional tax identification and complete tax formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT), using the applicable census registration process (Modelo 036) or notary-enabled electronic filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request the company's provisional NIF using the executed deed and register the company for the relevant tax census and activities. Incorporation is generally exempt from transfer tax and stamp duty under the applicable tax rules, but the required tax filing or exemption formalities must be confirmed and completed for the relevant Autonomous Community.
required_dossiers: Business activity and tax census information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistent activity, address, identity, or ownership data and resubmit the census declaration; provide the deed or supplementary information requested by AEAT or the competent regional tax authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company and obtain final NIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarial deed electronically through the notary where available, or file it with the Registry within the statutory period. Pay the applicable Registry charges. After registration, ensure the final NIF is obtained from AEAT and the company details are consistent across the deed, Registry record, and tax census.
required_dossiers: Tax identification and census filing evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Obtain and cure any Registry defect notice (nota de calificación), then resubmit the corrected instrument within the applicable cure period. If disputed, use the statutory Registry appeal process or execute a corrective deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration governance and employer registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company's governing body; AEAT; General Treasury of Social Security (Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social); and applicable regional and municipal administrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Record share ownership and corporate resolutions, keep required corporate books, and arrange legalization of books with the Commercial Registry under applicable rules. Register as an employer and obtain a contribution account code before employing staff. Make applicable tax, beneficial ownership, workplace, and local activity filings before commencing operations.
required_dossiers: Workplace and employer registration information, if hiring
Beneficial ownership and applicable tax filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct omitted or inconsistent corporate, tax, beneficial ownership, or Social Security filings with the relevant authority; pay applicable late charges and regularize before beginning regulated or employment activities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The competent Autonomous Community's industrial safety and industry authority (typically its Directorate-General for Industry or equivalent). There is no single national industrial licensing board. The competent municipality separately administers land-use compatibility, works, and activity or opening procedures.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific national manufacturing licence is generally prescribed solely for manufacturing overhead or gantry cranes. Before operation, the facility may require the Autonomous Community's industrial-establishment registration or notification under Royal Decree 559/2010, together with the applicable municipal activity/opening authorization and works permits. Machinery placed on the EU market must satisfy applicable EU product-safety and CE-conformity requirements.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: The competent environmental authority of the relevant Autonomous Community; the Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico) is the state-level authority where state competence applies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not automatically subject to a full EIA solely because the activity is crane manufacture. Screening under Law 21/2013 may be required if the specific facility, processes, capacity, location, or associated works fall within Annex I or Annex II or otherwise trigger assessment. Integrated environmental authorization applies only if the installation falls within the listed activities under applicable integrated-pollution-control legislation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No single sector-specific numerical threshold can be stated without the Autonomous Community, site, processes, and discharge destination. Obtain the required wastewater discharge authorization from the competent sewerage or water authority; comply with permit-specific limits and, for discharges to the public hydraulic domain, applicable water legislation. Assess VOC emissions and solvent use under Royal Decree 117/2003 where applicable; comply with installation-specific air-emission requirements. Classify, segregate, store, and transfer hazardous and non-hazardous waste through authorized channels under Law 7/2022 and applicable implementing rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain applicable municipal building and activity/opening approvals and any fire-safety reports required for the premises. The facility must meet the Spanish Building Code and applicable fire-protection rules, including Royal Decree 2267/2004 for industrial establishments. Structural design and floor or lifting-equipment loads must be verified by competent professionals against applicable building, machinery, and workplace requirements. Comply with Law 31/1995 on Occupational Risk Prevention, workplace rules under Royal Decree 486/1997, and machinery safety and inspection requirements applicable to installed lifting equipment. Specific certificates, inspections, and competent authorities depend on the Autonomous Community, municipality, premises, and equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic portal: sede.electronica.aeat.gob.es; NIF/VAT registration and advance valuation office: Departamento de Gestión Tributaria
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident investor forming a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a provisional NIF from AEAT before the public deed; after Mercantile Registry registration, the company files Form 036/037 to formalize its definitive corporate NIF, which also operates as the Spanish VAT registration number (NIF-IVA) for intra-EU transactions. A non-EU person without a permanent establishment must appoint a fiscal representative in Spain unless an exemption applies. The NIF application is accompanied by incorporation documents, Spanish power of attorney, and proof of identity; approval is generally obtained within days but may require translation/legalization.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SL is a Spanish resident juridical person taxed on worldwide income under the Ley del Impuesto sobre Sociedades (LIS); it is not eligible for pass-through treatment and cannot make a check-the-box election; transparency is reserved to certain civil vehicle types such as AIE/UTE, not to an SL.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box mechanism exists. An SL may elect: (i) tax consolidation under LIS arts. 62 et seq. for qualifying groups with the statutory majority shareholding and voting rights; (ii) the 15% reduced corporate tax rate as a newly created entity for the first two profitable tax periods if certain substance and capital conditions are met; (iii) application of special EU Merger Directive neutrality for reorganizations. Hybrid mismatch rules (ATAD) are mandatory and cannot be elected away; the SL may apply bilateral/multilateral APA regimes for transfer pricing but these are discretionary administrative rulings, not statutory elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA — Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (Spanish VAT/GST; mainland and Balearic Islands; Canary Islands applies IGIC instead of IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 / no general registration threshold. Any taxable person performing an economic activity in Spain must register for IVA before commencing operations irrespective of turnover. A EUR 250,000 annual turnover is only the statutory ceiling for access to the simplified VAT regime (régimen simplificado), not a registration exemption threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: AEAT imposes near-real-time VAT transactional records through the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) for taxpayers with annual turnover over EUR 6,000,000, consolidated groups, and taxpayers in the REDEME monthly-refund regime; invoice data must be sent to AEAT via certified web services/API within 4 working days (8 in exceptional cases). For all B2B invoicing, the Facturae XML electronic-invoice standard is mandatory under Law 18/2022 and its implementing regulation, with phased application based on turnover. The 'Verifactu' regime requires certified billing software to generate an immutable invoice delivery file (XML) with QR code and communicate issuances to AEAT, replacing paper stamping; no physical revenue stamp is necessary for ordinary invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exemption with credit (effective 0% VAT) applies to extra-EU exports under Ley 37/1992 arts. 21 and 22. Goods must leave EU customs territory through a valid export declaration and the exporter must prove the physical dispatch to a non-EU destination within the statutory time frame (ordinarily 90 days; up to 12 months for certain processing operations). Related international freight and transport services directly connected to the export also qualify. For gantry cranes delivered and installed outside the EU, the place of supply of goods is outside the EU, so no Spanish VAT is chargeable provided the evidence set is retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUI / Single Administrative Document) showing exit from EU customs territory
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill / CMR) evidencing physical delivery to a non-EU destination
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank proof that export proceeds have been received in Spain
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT cross-checks export declarations with customs exit data and transport manifests. If zero-rating is claimed without a real export or with fraudulent documents, the VAT is clawed back at 21% with late-payment interest (LGT art. 26) and graduated penalties under LGT arts. 191/194 of 50%-150%; intentional fraud may trigger criminal prosecution under Penal Code art. 305 when the annual amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 (1-5 years' imprisonment and a fine). Supporting records must be kept for at least 4 years, and abuse may lead to loss of REDEME monthly refund rights, VIES suspension, and customs exporter licensing revocation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain operates within the Eurozone capital account convertibility regime under EU free movement of capital rules, with unrestricted transfers of capital, profits, and dividends to non-resident shareholders. Current account transactions face no restrictions or prior approvals. Profit remittances are permitted subject only to standard 19% withholding tax on dividends and routine tax filings; no material convertibility hurdles exist for compliant Spanish SL entities engaged in cross-border trade.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spanish law imposes no mandatory surrender or central bank conversion of export proceeds. Exporters must submit customs declarations and file AEAT tax returns within 30 days of shipment. Foreign currency receipts may be retained in domestic or offshore accounts at the company's discretion, subject to AML reporting thresholds (EUR 10,000). Conversion to EUR is optional but required for operational liquidity management and to satisfy bank verification protocols.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for EU-regulated electronic money institutions under PSD2 and MiCA, enabling cross-border digital EMIs. Offshore digital EMIs remain subject to Banco de España licensing, correspondent banking restrictions, and enhanced AML controls for non-EU exposures.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for initial KYC interviews, director interviews, and document verification for Spanish SL entities. Remote video identification is permitted for subsequent transactions and qualifying SMEs using digital certificates, but first-time corporate onboarding typically requires in-person appearance at the bank branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP screening adverse hit on beneficial owners or directors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source of wealth and funds documentation, independent legal opinions confirming sanctions compliance, and third-party background verification reports

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media or negative credit history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited corporate and personal financial statements, third-party credit reports, and detailed explanations of mitigating factors

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are routed via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'CAP' or 'EQTY'. Verification requires shareholder resolutions, incorporation certificates, audited financial statements, and proof of funds origin. All transactions must reference the recipient IBAN and include a clear commercial description to satisfy bank and regulatory scrutiny.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for port container gantry crane exports utilize SWIFT MT103 for direct payments or issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit. Settlements proceed through correspondent banks with presentation of commercial invoices, packing lists, and bills of lading. Purpose codes such as 'TRADE' or specific export descriptions are applied.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward FX contracts for USD/EUR and other pairs
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for Latin American market exposures
Currency swaps for multi-period hedging of export receivables

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria – AEAT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers, from July 1 to July 25 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharges up to 20% of the tax liability, penalty interest at 3.75% plus late payment recargo of 5% per unpaid month, and administrative fines up to 150% of the tax base if declared incorrectly.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (Depósito de cuentas anuales) at the Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval at the Ordinary General Meeting; meeting must be held within the first six months of the fiscal year, so by July 31 for a December 31 year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines from 1,200 to 300,000 EUR depending on company size; registration of any subsequent corporate act is suspended until the deposit is made; repeated failure for three consecutive years leads to administrative strike-off and closure of the registry sheet.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit required if the company meets at least two of the following criteria for two consecutive fiscal years: total assets over €4,000,000; net annual turnover over €8,000,000; average headcount over 50 employees. Additional mandatory audit if the company is listed, part of a group, or operates in certain regulated sectors.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad, Real Decreto 1514/2007); consolidated financial statements apply EU-IFRS as adopted by the EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no separate annual UBO form in Spain; beneficial ownership data is recorded in the mandatory Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Libro Registro de Titularidades Reales) held at the company, and any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be updated within one month of the event. The annual accounts deposit includes a certification that the register is accurate and current as of the balance sheet date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Administradores)
Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Libro Registro de Titularidades Reales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: €500 – €2,500 per year for a professional registered office and corporate agent service in major cities
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: €2,000 – €6,000 per year for a medium-sized manufacturing entity meeting audit thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (general rate; 15% for newly-created entities in the first two tax periods with positive taxable income under Article 29.1 LIS)
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite for losses incurred from tax periods commencing on/after 1 January 2015; 18 years for pre-2016 losses (Ley 27/2014, art. 26)
